answer: Admission is salted retrieval: each identity gets a private salt and indexes a fixed public corpus. Each epoch the node draws forty random shards, salts them, and demands exact excerpts in ninety seconds. One index cannot answer for two identities: a farm must index N times (N disks, N bandwidth bills) or run N proxies in lockstep. A zephyr of sign-ups cannot hide in one copy. The corpus is the trellis each claimant must climb; each shard a walnut, cheap to glance at, costly to crack unread. Boundary: a funder who truly ingests it N times still passes. It prices headcount, never abolishes it.
